blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Consunji-led Semirara Mining and Power Corp. (SMPC) has denounced government rules requiring it to surrender its assets to participate in the highly anticipated coal bidding, saying they violate an existing law. The group dismissed the rule as “unfair,” claiming it “basically bars us from bidding.” READ: Semirara uncertainties deepen as DOE scraps 2026 coal auction “To require us to surrender ownership of our assets as a condition to bid is against Presidential Decree 972, a special law on coal mining, which clearly says that such assets are ours and we can remove them within one year from the […]... Keep on reading: SMPC: Coal bidding rule violates law
